---
title: "Approaches"
---

This section reviews 22 existing epi modeling frameworks, one document each on a shared template, plus brief notes on several more. It records how each one represents states, transitions, populations, networks, interventions, and time, and what the lingua franca should take or avoid. The reviews are the evidence for the rest of the project: [best-practices](../best-practices/README.md) distills them into recommendations, [design](../design/00-overview.md) turns those into a specification, and [examples](../examples/README.md) and [vignettes](../vignettes/README.md) test the design against real models from these frameworks.

## Key takeaways

The [full comparison](README.md) presents these as observations for `best-practices` to argue with, not conclusions.

- **Structural rigor and intervention expressiveness have not appeared together.** The best model specifications ([camdl](camdl.md), [odin](odin.md), [summer2](summer2.md), [epipack](epipack.md)) have essentially no intervention vocabulary; the best intervention vocabularies ([EMOD](emod.md), [EpiHiper](epihiper.md), [Starsim](starsim.md), [Atomica](atomica.md)) sit on weak or absent structural specification.
- **Typed rates, probabilities, and durations keep being reinvented.** Starsim, camdl, Atomica, and [EMULSION](emulsion.md) each distinguish them in a different medium; [EpiModel](epimodel.md) and odin show the errors that untyped time allows.
- **Transitions should be named data, and there are two kinds.** Where transitions are code (Starsim, EpiModel), a model cannot be diagrammed, checked, or converted. [EoN](eon.md), epipack, and EpiHiper independently separate spontaneous transitions from contact-mediated ones.
- **One specification under several paradigms has been demonstrated, but only partly.** camdl runs one text on three compartmental backends, epipack drives ODE and stochastic runs from one process list, and EMULSION switches between compartmental and individual-based with one keyword. Writing transmission so that mass-action, contact-matrix, and edge-based forms are one declaration is called the hardest unsolved problem, and EoN shows that network-to-compartmental conversion is a choice of closure.
- **Dwell-time distribution is an axis most frameworks silently fix as exponential.** [MEmilio](memilio.md) needs separate model families to span it; EpiHiper declares a distribution per transition.
- **A data format is a poor thing to write a model in.** EMULSION and [flepiMoP](flepimop.md) (YAML) and EMOD and EpiHiper (JSON) have good declarative semantics and hostile ergonomics. The reviews conclude that a readable grammar should sit on top of a canonical data serialization.
- **Interventions need declared eligibility, combination rules, and ordering.** EMOD and EpiHiper express who is targeted as data. [Vivarium](vivarium.md) and [epidemics](epidemics.md) state how overlapping effects combine. [individual](individual.md) makes within-step order irrelevant.
- **Structure should be specifiable by its generating model.** EpiModel fits networks from target statistics, and [LASER](laser.md) ships named mobility models.

## Framework reviews

| Framework | Language | Paradigm(s) | What to learn from it |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Starsim](starsim.md) | Python | Agent-based (primary), network, metapopulation, ODE-style compartmental | Typed time, per-module timesteps, common random numbers, and one `Route` for networks and mixing pools; transitions and connectors are still code. |
| [EpiModel](epimodel.md) | R | ODE, stochastic random mixing, dynamic network (TERGM) | Contact networks fitted from target statistics and diagnosed before use; a parallel `param`/`init`/`control` API across three model classes; untyped time as the cautionary part. |
| [camdl](camdl.md) | camdl DSL (OCaml, Rust) | Compartmental: ODE, chain-binomial, Gillespie | Dimensional types checked before a run, named transitions as data, one model text on three backends, and a declarative observation block. |
| [odin](odin.md) | R DSL generating C++ | ODE, discrete-time stochastic | Order-independent equations, `zero_every` accumulators for incidence, a likelihood in the model file, and a language/engine/inference split. |
| [summer2](summer2.md) | Python (JAX) | Compartmental: ODE, stochastic | Stratification as a validated transformation of a finished model, made possible by a closed vocabulary of named flow kinds. |
| [MEmilio](memilio.md) | C++, Python bindings | ODE, IDE, LCT, SDE, metapopulation, agent-based, hybrid | Paradigms form a lattice with dwell time as one axis; each family is a separate implementation, which shows what a shared specification would save. |
| [EMULSION](emulsion.md) | YAML DSL (Python engine) | Compartmental, individual-based, hybrid, metapopulation | One keyword switches the same model between compartmental and individual-based; rate, probability, or duration per transition. The switch's limits are undocumented. |
| [epymorph](epymorph.md) | Python (SymPy) | Metapopulation | Disease, movement, and geography as independent parts, with declared, typed, shaped data requirements bound separately. |
| [MetaCast](metacast.md) | Python | Metapopulation ODE | Stratification and metapopulation structure as one dimension operation, with transfers between coordinates and a framework-computed force of infection. |
| [Epydemix](epydemix.md) | Python | Compartmental: stochastic, deterministic | `spontaneous`/`mediated` transition kinds that users can extend, calendar dates throughout, and bundled population and contact data. |
| [epipack](epipack.md) | Python (SymPy) | Compartmental: ODE, stochastic, network | One reaction-tuple list drives ODE, Gillespie, and symbolic analysis; the network mode needs a separate vocabulary, so the unification is incomplete. |
| [EMOD](emod.md) | C++ engine, JSON models | Agent-based with node-level metapopulation | A four-part campaign grammar (where, when and how many, to whom, what) with declarative targeting and waning; the disease model itself is not specifiable. |
| [epiworld](epiworld.md) | C++ core; R and Python bindings | Agent-based: network, fully connected, mixing matrix | One engine with identical semantics in two host languages; viruses and tools as agent-attached objects with multiplicative effects. |
| [individual](individual.md) | R, C++ core | Agent-based, discrete time | The minimal primitive set, with queued updates that make process order within a step irrelevant. |
| [SimInf](siminf.md) | R, generated C | Stochastic compartmental (Gillespie) on a network of nodes | Readable transition strings, scheduled events driven by real movement data, and discrete and continuous state side by side. |
| [Atomica](atomica.md) | Python engine, Excel models | Deterministic compartmental, cascades, budget optimization | A non-programmer specification path: transition matrix, parameter `Format` column, characteristics, and programs with costs. |
| [EoN](eon.md) | Python (NetworkX) | Stochastic network simulation plus analytic ODE approximations | The model as two directed graphs, and a runnable ladder of approximations for measuring what each closure assumption loses. |
| [flepiMoP](flepimop.md) | Python and R, YAML config | Metapopulation compartmental with inference | A whole workflow in one document, with chainable outcomes (source, probability, delay, duration) and a modifier grammar for interventions and scenarios. |
| [EpiHiper](epihiper.md) | C++, JSON models | Agent-based on explicit contact networks | Disease model and interventions both as data: per-transition dwell-time distributions and a sets/variables/triggers/operations rule language, in very verbose JSON. |
| [Vivarium](vivarium.md) | Python | Agent-based microsimulation | Value pipelines (one producer, registered modifiers, a declared combiner), a named lifecycle, and declared read/write access to state. |
| [LASER](laser.md) | Python, Numba | Spatial agent-based, discrete time | A library of spatial-interaction models and stated performance principles, as a contrast with Starsim's design choices. |
| [epidemics](epidemics.md) | R (odin) | Deterministic compartmental; one stochastic model | The opposite choice: fixed model structures with composable scenario elements, and a written design-principles document that states its composition rule. |

## Where to go for detail

[README.md](README.md) is the full comparison: the landscape table, the selection process and exclusions, and all twelve cross-cutting findings. [notes.md](notes.md) has brief entries for frameworks without a full review, including Mesa, Catalyst.jl, SBML, and ASKEM AMR / MIRA.
